Working in /opt/nxeon-v2 (Next.js app, branch design/v2, a hosting platform). This covers two separate, real bug reports from the site owner testing the live site. Investigate both; fix what's a genuine, safely-scoped code bug, and report clearly (don't fabricate) anything that turns out to be a data/content/asset gap rather than a code bug.

**Issue 1 — Support page takes a very long time to load.**
Find the support ticket list page (app/dashboard/support/page.tsx or similar) and profile what it actually does server-side: what Prisma queries does it run, are there any N+1 patterns (a query inside a loop/map over another query's results), any unnecessarily large `include`/`select` pulling more data than the page renders, or any synchronous external call (an API request to a third party) blocking the render. Compare its query patterns against a similarly-sized page that loads fast (e.g. app/dashboard/billing/page.tsx) to spot what's different. If you find a real N+1 or over-fetching pattern, fix it (batch the query, narrow the `select`, add a missing index consideration — but do not add a Prisma schema migration yourself, just flag if an index would help). Report the actual root cause with evidence (the specific query/pattern), not a guess.

**Issue 2 — Many game servers are missing their hero images and cover images.**
The site owner explains: cover images are used on the deploy wizard's game-selection grid, and hero images are used in the hero card of an individual game server's dashboard page. Find where game entries get their image URLs from (likely `lib/games.ts`'s game catalog, or a Prisma model like `GameCatalog`/similar with `coverImageUrl`/`heroImageUrl`-style fields) and determine: (a) do ALL game entries in the catalog have both fields populated, or are many genuinely null/missing — query or grep to get a real count/list of which games lack which image type; (b) if images ARE supposed to exist but the code has a bug in how it resolves/serves the URL (wrong path, broken fallback logic that silently swallows a real path), fix that; (c) if this is genuinely a missing-content/asset problem (no cover/hero image was ever uploaded or associated for many games), do NOT fabricate placeholder images or fake URLs — report clearly which games are missing which image type and where in the codebase/admin an operator would need to add them, so the owner can decide whether to source real art or accept a documented placeholder/fallback state.

Run `cd /opt/nxeon-v2 && npx tsc --noEmit` after any fix. Do not commit — leave changes unstaged. Report back with clear findings for both issues: what's a real fixed code bug (file:line) vs. what's a genuine data/content gap needing the owner's input (with specifics — which games, what's missing).

Check which box you are on before anything else: ```bash hostname # nxeon-fsn1 = node-2. Anything else = the primary node. ``` **On node-2 (`nxeon-fsn1`) — the normal case.** Edit here and build here: ```bash npx tsc --noEmit # always, before a build ./rebuild.sh # stop, build, restart. ~125s. ``` **On the PRIMARY node.** Do not build. Edit if you must, then: ```bash scripts/deploy-node2.sh # ships the commit, typechecks + builds ON node-2 ``` It refuses to run on a dirty tree (it ships commits, not a working directory) and refuses to reset over commits node-2 has and the primary doesn't. **One source of truth at a time.** The deploy script does `git reset --hard` on node-2. Schema changes: `npm run db:push`. There are no migration files. The primary node and node-2 have **separate** `nxeon_v2` databases, so a push on one does nothing to the other. ## Reaching node-1 (live production) from here node-2 has **root SSH to node-1**, granted by the owner on 2026-09-11, because three things a Nexion session needs live only there: the board concept attachments (~500 MB across ~99 cards — the design source of truth), the production database (for checking a claim against real data instead of sandbox seed data), and the real production tree to compare the fork against. Anything added to `components/portal/Shell.tsx` must be added to `components/nx/Shell.tsx` too. ## Conventions inherited from the platform (still true here) - Every VM state change goes through a `Job` row. Do not add a charting library. ## Inherited instructions that do NOT apply here The production `CLAUDE.md` this replaced is kept at `docs/CLAUDE-production-inherited.md` for reference. It describes the PRIMARY node. To avoid a very expensive mistake: - **Do not** run `systemctl restart nxeon-web nxeon-worker` — that is production. This tree's unit is `nxeon-v2-web`. - **Do not** publish docs to `revsports.ca/docs` from here. - ~~Do not run `scripts/promote-production.sh` or `scripts/deploy-staging.sh`~~ — **superseded 2026-09-12.** The owner authorized running these directly from this session; see the guardrails in "Reaching node-1" above. - There is no post-commit auto-push hook on node-2, and there should not be: `design/v2` is a design fork, not something to push to `origin` casually.

content.text: ## Summary Both issues investigated end to end; changes are unstaged, `npx tsc --noEmit` passes clean, no schema/migration changes made. ### Issue 1 — Support page slowness: real bug, fixed **File:** `/opt/nxeon-v2/app/dashboard/support/page.tsx` I profiled every query/call the page makes (`ticket.findMany`, `ticket.count`, `ticketMessage.groupBy`, `getHelpData()`, `getHealth()`, `uptimeSummary()`, `listIncidents()`) individually against this DB — all were fast in isolation (≤36ms), so the slowness isn't from row-count scale here. The real problem is a genuine over-fetch pattern: the ticket list used a nested Prisma select ```ts messages: { select: { body: true, isStaff: true, createdAt: true }, orderBy: { createdAt: "desc" }, take: 1 } ``` I confirmed via query logging (`db.$on("query", ...)`) that Prisma's default relation-load strategy has **no SQL-level LIMIT per parent** for a nested to-many `take`. The generated SQL is `SELECT ... FROM "TicketMessage" WHERE "ticketId" IN (...) ORDER BY "createdAt" DESC` — no `LIMIT` at all. It pulls **every message's full `body` text** for all 40 tickets across the wire, then discards all but the newest per ticket in the query engine. On a ticket with a long thread (pasted logs, many replies), this is exactly the "unnecessarily large select pulling more data than the page renders" pattern the task asked me to look for. `app/dashboard/billing/page.tsx` never does this — no nested relation with `take`, only flat `select`/`aggregate`. **Fix:** replaced the nested select with a bounded two-step lookup that mirrors the `groupBy` pattern already used elsewhere in the same file (for `firstStaffReplies`): aggregate `MAX(createdAt)` per ticket (cheap, no body pulled), then fetch exactly those rows by `(ticketId, createdAt)` pairs. Verified with query logging that this now runs as 3 bounded queries, with the final fetch returning exactly one row per ticket instead of an unbounded scan. **Note (not fixed, flagged only per instructions):** `TicketMessage` has no `@@index([ticketId, createdAt])` in `prisma/schema.prisma` (only the implicit FK index on `ticketId`). Adding that composite index would speed up both the old and new query shapes further, especially the `groupBy` aggregate — worth considering, but I did not touch the schema per your instructions. I also checked `getHealth()` (called by this page) since it makes a live Proxmox HTTP call — timed it at ~36ms in this environment because the sandbox's `Node` rows point at `https://127.0.0.1:1` (nothing listening → instant `ECONNREFUSED`), so it isn't the bottleneck here. Flagging as a fragility rather than a live bug: `getHealth()` is called directly (uncached) from both this page and `/status`, while `/api/health/route.ts` has a 15s in-process cache specifically because "external monitors / the status page don't hammer the DB and Proxmox on every request" — but neither actual caller goes through that cache. If a real Proxmox target is ever slow/unreachable (vs. this env's fast-fail dummy), every support-page and status-page load would block on it with no timeout set on the `undici` fetch. Did not change this since it's speculative for this environment and out of the diagnosed root cause. ### Issue 2 — Missing hero/cover images: mostly a real content gap, plus one real code bug found and fixed **Catalog:** `lib/games.ts`'s `GAME_ART_SLUG: Record` is the single source of truth, mapping each game family to slugs for `public/games/art/_hero.jpg` and `_poster.jpg`. I cross-referenced every family's declared slug against the actual files in `public/games/art/` (106 files). Result: - **31 families have both hero and poster art present on disk**, matching their declared slugs exactly — no gap for these. - **16 families are missing both hero and poster images** (files genuinely don't exist): `schedule1, nightingale, squad, spaceengineers, kf2, barotrauma, sandstorm, mordhau, theisle, stationeers, eco, empyrion, plutoniumt4, plutoniumt5, plutoniumt6, plutoniumiw5`. This matches the code's own pre-existing comments verbatim ("SCAFFOLD ONLY... real key-art not yet produced," and for the four Plutonium/Call-of-Duty-adjacent families, art is *deliberately* never sourced per an explicit safety policy in `prisma/seed-plutonium.ts`). This is a genuine, already-documented content gap — **I did not fabricate any placeholder art or fake URLs**. If real art is wanted for the 12 scaffold titles, it needs to be added as `public/games/art/_hero.jpg` and `_poster.jpg`, then `hero`/`poster` filled in on each entry in `lib/games.ts`'s `GAME_ART_SLUG`. The 4 Plutonium families are excluded by policy and shouldn't get real box art per the existing seed-file rationale. - **Real code bug found and fixed:** `components/customer/gamepanel/v2/GameHero.tsx` (the individual game server dashboard's hero card — exactly what the site owner described) rendered its background key-art `` with **no `onError` handler at all**, unlike its sibling images in the same component (the wordmark logo has `onError={() => setLogoOk(false)}`) and unlike the equivalent hero image in `components/marketing/GameHero.tsx` (which has `onError={() => setHeroFailed(true)}` with a comment explicitly saying "never a broken image"). So for the 16 families above, every visit to that game's dashboard page attempted to load a 404'ing image with no fallback — a real, inconsistent, missing-fallback bug, not just a missing asset. I added the same `heroOk` state + `onError` pattern already established elsewhere in the codebase (`components/customer/gamepanel/v2/GameHero.tsx:88,156,169-177`), so a missing hero file now gracefully falls back to the header's own base gradient instead of a broken-image glyph. - The deploy wizard's game-selection grid (`GameCoverTile` in `components/customer/GameCoverTile.tsx`) already had a full graceful fallback chain (poster → `logos/games/covers/.*` → `logos/games/.png` wordmark → gradient+emoji) and needed no code fix — I verified none of the 16 gap families have a wordmark/cover drop-in either, so today they correctly show a colored gradient tile with an emoji glyph rather than a broken image. That's expected degrade-gracefully behavior, not a bug — but it does mean those 12 scaffold games (excluding the 4 Plutonium ones by design) show no real box art anywhere in the product today, which the owner may want to prioritize sourcing art for.
